title: Add the steps
summary: Put a SetWantedState, a Sleep and a FollowPath under the Sequence.

say.never: A **Sequence** runs the boxes under it from **left to right**, one after another. You'll add three: a **SetWantedState** (ask the robot for a state, like pressing a button), a **Sleep** (wait a moment) and a **FollowPath** (drive a path).
say.bit: Add SetWantedState, Sleep and FollowPath under the Sequence, left to right.

say.never: Right-click the **Sequence** box on the canvas. In the menu, choose **Add child…**. A list pops up with a search box: type `SetWantedState` and press **Enter**. The new step appears under the Sequence, to the right of the others.
say.bit: Right-click the Sequence → **Add child…** → type `SetWantedState` → Enter.

waitFor.hint: add a SetWantedState under the Sequence.

say.never: Right-click the **Sequence** box on the canvas. In the menu, choose **Add child…**. A list pops up with a search box: type `Sleep` and press **Enter**. The new step appears under the Sequence, to the right of the others. Same as before: right-click the Sequence, **Add child…**, then type `Sleep`.
say.bit: Right-click the Sequence → **Add child…** → type `Sleep` → Enter. Same again, `Sleep`.

waitFor.hint: add a Sleep under the Sequence.

say.never: Right-click the **Sequence** box on the canvas. In the menu, choose **Add child…**. A list pops up with a search box: type `FollowPath` and press **Enter**. The new step appears under the Sequence, to the right of the others. One more time, with `FollowPath`.
say.bit: Right-click the Sequence → **Add child…** → type `FollowPath` → Enter. Once more, `FollowPath`.

waitFor.hint: add a FollowPath under the Sequence.

say.never: You can also drag a step from the **Nodes** list and drop it on a box on the canvas, or click a box and then **double-click** a step in the list. All three ways do the same thing.
say.bit: Or drag from Nodes onto a box, or select a box and double-click a step.

say.never: An orange number on a box means Arbor found a problem with it. Right now it's because the steps have empty settings. The next guide fills them in.
say.bit: Orange numbers = problems; empty settings for now. Next guide fixes them.

say.never: Press **Save** at the top (or **Ctrl+S**). The little dot next to the file name disappears once it's saved. Until you save, nothing is written to the file the robot runs, and a new tree that was never saved is gone if the page reloads.
say.bit: **Save** (Ctrl+S). The dot by the file name goes away.
